target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN returned response headers and then dripped the audio body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body — including non-2xx error-detail reads inside shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`, one wall-clock deadline now spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` / `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching the Vydra / Discord probe hang-floor shape.

Header fetch still goes through `fetchProviderOperationResponse` (keeps transient download retries). `requestFailedMessage` is omitted on purpose so shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` cannot consume a dripping error body without a wall-clock bound before this helper's timed readers run.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset` / `src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts`.

## User Impact

Generated music URL downloads fail within the configured timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing — for both 2xx asset bodies and dripping non-2xx error bodies. Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 278ms
 ✓ bounds a dripping non-2xx error body with one wall-clock deadline 256ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 407ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Loopback proof

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-music-download-deadline.mts
```

```
head=ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac
node=v22.22.0
  ok: drip body (200) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: error mentions timeoutMs
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=200-drip elapsed_ms=261 timeout_ms=250
  ok: drip error body (500) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=500-drip elapsed_ms=253 timeout_ms=250
  ok: negative control: idle-only on drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control settled=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous 20ms chunk drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 261ms — wall-clock deadline covers body, not just headers.
- **Drip non-2xx body (500)**: continuous 20ms drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 253ms — error-detail body reads also bounded.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms — proves the old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.title: fix(clawhub): keep request deadline through response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where ClawHub request deadlines were cleared at HTTP headers, leaving stalled or dripping response bodies unbounded. Fixes a compatibility issue where the previous revision applied the same 30s wall-clock deadline to large (up to 256 MiB) archive downloads, which could terminate a healthy progressing transfer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clawhubRequest` previously cleared its `AbortController` timer as soon as `fetch` returned headers, so `readResponseWithLimit` per-chunk idle detection was the only body bound — a slow drip could keep resetting chunk-idle and hang forever.

This change keeps the wall-clock deadline through body consumption for all paths, but archive downloads (`downloadClawHubPackageArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchiveUrl`, `downloadClawHubGitHubSkillArchive`) release it after headers via a new `releaseAfterHeaders` option. Per-chunk idle detection in `readClawHubResponseBytes` still bounds stalls for all paths.

Non-goals: changing `readClawHubResponseBytes` or `readResponseWithLimit` internals, changing the default 30s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `src/infra/clawhub.ts` with overlapping deadline semantics.

## User Impact

- Stalled or continuously dripping ClawHub metadata/JSON responses fail with the request wall-clock deadline instead of hanging.
- Archive downloads (skill, package, ClawPack, GitHub source) are not cut off at the 30s metadata budget; a progressing transfer completes while per-chunk idle detection still terminates stalled bodies.
- Retry, error-body, and JSON paths keep the full-body wall-clock.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ecb99af3b605822264d8e0c1d8a76db8f8dcd026`

`oxfmt --check src/infra/clawhub.ts src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/clawhub.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > keeps the ClawHub request deadline through stalled bodies after headers 53ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > aborts ClawHub JSON bodies that drip past the request deadline 52ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled skill archive body reads 11ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled package archive body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled ClawPack artifact body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > lets a progressing archive body survive past the request deadline 6ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  83 passed | 2 skipped (85)
```

### Contract

| Path | Wall-clock | Chunk-idle | Stall bound |
|------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| Metadata/JSON (`fetchJson`, `parseClawHubJsonBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Error bodies (`readErrorBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Skill card (`fetchClawHubSkillCard`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Promotions feed (`fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| **Archive downloads** | **released at headers** | 30s | **chunk-idle** |

### New test: progressing archive survives past request deadline

- `downloadClawHubSkillArchive` with `timeoutMs: 50`, `releaseAfterHeaders: true`, body drips every 10ms (10 chunks) via fake timers
- `abortCount: 0` — request deadline was not triggered
- Transfer completes with valid `sha256Hex` — progressing body not falsely terminated

### Not tested

Live ClawHub CDN against real archive endpoints — requires real ClawHub auth token.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750
Follow-up: #105877

## Current Status

The implementation and validation work is complete on the frozen final range:

```text
base: ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d
head: edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

The branch intentionally stays on that reviewed and verified baseline. It will not continue chasing later `main` movement. GitHub currently reports the PR as `CONFLICTING / DIRTY` because `main` advanced again after the final rebase; that repository-level conflict is the only known landability blocker.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart could repeatedly select the same interrupted main session for automatic recovery. The existing retry loop was process-local, so supervisor backoff only delayed the next attempt: a session that never became healthy could be dispatched again after every restart without a durable ceiling.

This PR adds a durable, session-owned recovery fuse. The first three accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recovery attempts may dispatch. Before a fourth dispatch, OpenClaw persists an operator notice, tombstones the session, and requires recovery through inspection and `/new` or reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Recovery ownership

The durable state is the core-internal `InternalSessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` aggregate, separate from the public `SessionEntry` contract. It records the recovery cycle and revision, charged attempts, the exact pre-dispatch reservation, lifecycle-generation foreground claim tokens, and an optional terminal tombstone.

`src/agents/main-session-recovery-state.ts` owns the pure transitions. `src/agents/main-session-recovery-store.ts` owns atomic persistence against the canonical SQLite row. Gateway and direct agent-command ingress use the same identity, revision, reservation, lifecycle-generation, and foreground-owner rules.

The policy is:

- persist the charge and reservation before dispatch;
- roll back only when the exact request is known not to have been accepted;
- retain the charge when acceptance is uncertain, including a stale reservation after restart;
- allow three charged attempts, then persist the notice and tombstone before a fourth dispatch;
- do not reset the budget merely because time passes; and
- clear it after healthy non-aborted settlement, session replacement, or reset.

`restartRecoveryRuns` remains a lifecycle-generation fence rather than the durable retry budget. Subagent orphan recovery remains independently owned and retains its existing policy.

### Concurrency and restart safety

The final implementation includes:

- lifecycle-generation fences so stale cleanup cannot erase new work;
- Gateway recovery leases bound to the exact recovery identity;
- snapshot revision and foreground-claim checks around concurrent admission;
- stale lifecycle-clear suppression after tombstoning;
- predecessor preclaims during freshness rollover;
- exact reservation rollback across session-key canonicalization; and
- transcript-only exhaustion notice persistence before tombstoning, with retry when notice persistence fails.

### Plugin SDK boundary

Recovery coordination remains internal and does not become a plugin contract.

- Public session reads project internal rows to `SessionEntry`.
- Modern patch/upsert APIs strip escaped private input and preserve internal recovery state.
- Deprecated `loadSessionStore` and `updateSessionStore` now also project public rows and reconcile public mutations while preserving private recovery state and deletion semantics.
- The public testing result excludes the internal recovery candidate.
- The generated Plugin SDK surface contains no recovery-internal concept, and no checksum-only baseline update hides a semantic change.

The broader shipped Plugin SDK testing-barrel question remains tracked separately in #105877.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three charged accepted or acceptance-uncertain attempts, OpenClaw persists the operator notice and quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch. Healthy progress, replacement, or reset restores the full budget; waiting alone does not.

Plugins continue to see the public session contract and cannot observe or accidentally overwrite the internal recovery state through either modern or deprecated session-store APIs.

## Evidence

Exact frozen range:

```text
ee80377a22b36b1bff6faed20c9233134e2a186d..edc24088387a8d573798233979a71f3b40a24ac9
```

- Focused final regression set: 227 tests passed (`14` recovery-state, `15` Gateway lifecycle, `198` agent tests).
- Broader restart-recovery suite: 86 passed.
- Agent-command suite: 112 passed.
- Core production and test `tsgo` lanes passed.
- Targeted and changed-file `oxfmt` / `oxlint` passed.
- LOC ratchet passed for all 53 changed production TypeScript files.
- Full changed-file gate passed against the frozen base, including core/extension types, lint, Plugin SDK surface/API/exports, and repository guards.
- Full local build passed on Node `24.15.0`.
- Mandatory default-Codex Auto Review covered the final change in six synthetic slices plus the final dirty follow-up; no accepted/actionable finding remains.
- Thread-aware GitHub inspection found no unresolved inline review threads; the current maintainer review decision is `APPROVED`.

Final end-to-end proof used a local Docker container, actual provider `local-container`, lease `cbx_9736f8111fa1`, Ubuntu 26.04:

- complete container build passed;
- a real Gateway started successfully;
- exhausted recovery ended with `status=failed`, `abortedLastRun=false`, and `chargedAttempts=3`;
- the transcript notice was persisted; and
- the tombstone was written before any fourth dispatch.

Exact-head GitHub automation has passed the dependency and security guards plus one real-behavior proof run. The standard full CI workflow did not dispatch for this fork-head update. Exact-merge-result CI cannot exist while GitHub reports the later-main conflict.

## Known Blocker

The code, tests, review findings, and exact-head behavior proof are complete. GitHub currently reports `mergeable=CONFLICTING` and `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` after `main` advanced again. Per the frozen-branch decision, this PR will not be rebased or merged with another moving `main` baseline.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 12:09 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:09 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 16, 2026, 11:58 PM (US Eastern Time) / 03:58 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 04:00 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@06295d97214c83a8e72fbcd763792b4011d301d8`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`
- focused gateway session/startup and subagent tests selected by changed-file CI
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/agents/command/model-selection.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Evidence Source Map

- Exact-head downstream CI: [Evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29553799447)
  - Head: `06295d97214c83a8e72fbcd763792b4011d301d8`
  - Base: `ff9b29167352b5896c772dfcff9176fb003f530d`
  - Conclusion: in progress
  - Covers focused unit tests, changed-file checks, formatting, type checks, and
    regression lanes selected by the repository workflow.
- Draft-state upstream PR CI: [PR workflow run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29554005118)
  - Conclusion: skipped as expected while the PR is Draft; a full PR run will replace this entry before review is requested.

## Sanitized Logs

```text
Merged config: listed agent without thinkingDefault -> global value
Explicit override: listed agent thinkingDefault=off -> off
Precedence guard: listed agent without override + per-model thinking + global default -> per-model value
git diff --check -> passed
```

No credentials, hostnames, internal paths, account identifiers, or private
runtime data are included.

## Media Evidence

This is a non-visual configuration-resolution change. The linked Actions run
provides the complete reproducible source-level flow and exact-head result;
there is no UI state or dynamic interaction for a screenshot or recording to
clarify.

## Risk

- Compatibility: callers that intentionally inspect merged config now observe
  the documented global fallback.
- Precedence: mitigated by keeping explicit agent provenance in a dedicated
  helper and by regression coverage for per-model-over-global behavior.
- Performance: one normalized agent-entry lookup replaces an equivalent config
  lookup at the affected callers; no new I/O or runtime catalog loading.
- Security/privacy: no authorization, secret, persistence, or transport changes.

target.title: fix(config-cli,secrets): typed ExitError, JSON error output, and consistent stateDir for audit .env
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

### config get --json

`openclaw config get <path> --json` produces empty stdout when the config path does not exist. It only writes a text error message to stderr and exits with code 1. Automated consumers (scripts, CI) that pipe stdout expecting JSON receive nothing, making error handling unreliable.

### Secrets audit & apply .env path

The secrets audit and apply operations resolve the state directory for auth/model stores but re-resolve it for `.env`. If directory availability changes between calls (canonical `.openclaw` vs legacy `.clawdbot` directory appearing or disappearing), one operation can inspect or mutate two different state roots for the same run.

In `apply.ts` specifically, `projectPlanState` resolves `stateDir` once and uses it for config targets, auth stores, and legacy auth stores — but `scrubEnvFiles` calls `resolveStateDir` independently, so a root switch mid-operation can scrub a different `.env` and leave the intended plaintext credential untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

### config get --json

The `--json` flag implies machine-readable output on stdout. When a path is not found, the command now emits a structured JSON error on stdout, consistent with how `runConfigValidate` and `handleConfigMutationError` handle JSON-mode errors. The exit signal detection was also migrated from a fragile `__exit__:` string prefix match to the repository's typed `ExitError` contract.

### Secrets audit .env path

Reuse the already-resolved `stateDir` variable for constructing the `.env` path in `audit.ts`.

### Secrets apply .env path

Pass the `stateDir` already resolved by `projectPlanState` (line 296) into `scrubEnvFiles` instead of letting `scrubEnvFiles` call `resolveStateDir` again. This ensures auth stores (auth-profiles.json, auth.json) and `.env` are handled under the same state root for the entire apply operation.

## User Impact

- `openclaw config get nonexistent.path --json` now outputs `{"error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"}` to stdout (exit code 1)
- Non-JSON mode behavior is unchanged: error goes to stderr as before
- Secrets audit consistently reads `.env` from the same state directory as auth and model stores
- Secrets apply scrubs `.env` under the same state root as auth stores — no root-switch gap

## Evidence

### Real CLI proof — config get --json

**stdout:**
```
{
  "error": "Config path not found: nonexistent.path"
}
```
**stderr:** (build bootstrap logs only, no config command error output)
```
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs config get nonexistent.path --json
[openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: dirty_watched_tree - dirty watched source tree).
...
```
**Exit code:** 1

### Real CLI proof — secrets audit

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE_DIR pnpm openclaw secrets audit --json
{
  "version": 1,
  "status": "findings",
  "filesScanned": [
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/.env",
    "/tmp/.../openclaw/openclaw.json"
  ],
  "summary": { "plaintextCount": 2, ... },
  "findings": [
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw.json", ... },
    { "code": "PLAINTEXT_FOUND", "file": ".../openclaw/.env", "jsonPath": "$env.OPENAI_API_KEY", ... }
  ]
}
```
Exit code: 0

### Real CLI proof — secrets apply (root-switch)

**Setup:** HOME contains both `.openclaw` (canonical) and `.clawdbot` (legacy) directories. Both have `.env` files with plaintext keys, plus `openclaw.json` with a plaintext `apiKey`.

**Before apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (canonical, SHOULD be scrubbed) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (legacy, must NOT be touched) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": "sk-prod-plaintext-should-be-scrubbed"
```

**Command:**
```
$ HOME=$TMPHOME pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from plan.json
Secrets applied. Updated 2 file(s).
```

**After apply:**
```
-- .openclaw/.env (verify scrubbed) --
UNRELATED=keep-me

-- .clawdbot/.env (verify UNTOUCHED) --
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-legacy-should-NOT-be-touched
UNRELATED=legacy-value

-- openclaw.json --
"apiKey": {
  "source": "env",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
}
```

**Verification:**
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (plaintext key removed)
- ✅ `.openclaw/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=keep-me`
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (legacy key still present)
- ✅ `.clawdbot/.env` preserved `UNRELATED=legacy-value`
- ✅ `openclaw.json` plaintext `apiKey` replaced with `SecretRef`

The plan targets `models.providers.openai.apiKey` with `scrubEnv: true`. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both directories exist, and the apply operation uses that single resolved `stateDir` for both auth stores and `.env` scrubbing. The legacy `.clawdbot/.env` is never touched.

### Tests

- `pnpm test src/secrets/apply.test.ts` — **31/31 passed** (includes new root-switch regression: "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores")
- `pnpm test src/secrets/audit.test.ts` — **26/26 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — **130/130 passed**
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts` — **5/5 passed**

### Lint & Format

- oxlint: clean (`src/secrets/apply.ts`, `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`)
- oxfmt: clean

### New regression test — apply root-switch

The test sets up a HOME where both `.openclaw` and `.clawdbot` exist. `resolveStateDir` returns `.openclaw` when both exist (it checks `.openclaw` first). The test:

1. Writes a `.env` with a plaintext secret in `.openclaw` (canonical)
2. Writes a different `.env` with a dummy secret in `.clawdbot` (legacy)
3. Runs `secrets apply` with `scrubEnv: true`
4. Asserts `.openclaw/.env` was scrubbed (secret removed)
5. Asserts `.clawdbot/.env` was NOT touched (secret still present)

This proves one apply operation cannot switch roots mid-operation.

### Review findings addressed (revise round)

- **[P2] Reuse the operation's resolved state directory in apply** — `src/secrets/apply.ts:734`: `scrubEnvFiles` now accepts `stateDir` parameter and uses it instead of calling `resolveStateDir` again. Call site at line 341 passes the `stateDir` resolved on line 296.
- **[P1] Add root-switch regression** — `src/secrets/apply.test.ts`: New test "uses the same resolved stateDir for .env scrubbing as for auth stores" proves the invariant.

### Behavior addressed

- CLI JSON errors now reliably reach stdout consumers
- Exit signal contract migrated from `__exit__:` string sentinel to typed `ExitError`
- Audit `.env` lookup uses resolved `stateDir` instead of re-resolving
- Apply `.env` scrubbing uses the same `stateDir` as auth stores — single-root invariant

### What was not tested

- macOS-specific `realpath` symlink behavior (Linux CI parity)

target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with DashScope-compatible video downloads:

1. **Stalled CDN body hang**: After headers returned, no chunk-idle timeout was wired into `readResponseWithLimit`, so a stalled body could wait the full request budget instead of failing with a clear idle timeout.
2. **Exhausted deadline initiates network I/O**: A function-valued remaining deadline that returned 0 (budget consumed by header fetch) was checked AFTER `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` had already sent bytes over the wire. The guard now runs before fetch.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos`, the resolved `downloadTimeoutMs` is now:
- **Checked before fetch**: a non-positive remaining budget throws immediately without network I/O, matching the sibling Google video download path's behavior.
- **Passed as `chunkTimeoutMs`** + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, so stalled bodies fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` deadline.

`fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever; the chunk-idle bound is the download-owned stall signal that was missing.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, `readResponseWithLimit`, or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

Collision check: no open PR on `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` / `src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts`.

## User Impact

- Stalled DashScope video downloads fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic request timeout or full-budget wait.
- Already-exhausted remaining budgets fail immediately without network I/O.
- Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `920b47be7e9a11c1fbb78845226d51aca97afdf8`

`oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 511ms
 ✓ persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 5ms
 ✓ fails closed before fetch when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 5ms
 ✓ bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 220ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Key contract changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Exhausted deadline checked after `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` (network I/O already initiated) | Checked before fetch — throws immediately, `fetchFn` not called |
| Body had no chunk-idle timeout → stalled bodies hit generic request timeout | `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` wired → `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` |

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` returns HTTP 200 + one chunk then stalls. Real `fetch` + real `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` with `timeoutMs: 200` rejects within 5s (~220ms observed) — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: low

target.title: fix(clawhub): keep request deadline through response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where ClawHub request deadlines were cleared at HTTP headers, leaving stalled or dripping response bodies unbounded. Fixes a compatibility issue where the previous revision applied the same 30s wall-clock deadline to large (up to 256 MiB) archive downloads, which could terminate a healthy progressing transfer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clawhubRequest` previously cleared its `AbortController` timer as soon as `fetch` returned headers, so `readResponseWithLimit` per-chunk idle detection was the only body bound — a slow drip could keep resetting chunk-idle and hang forever.

This change keeps the wall-clock deadline through body consumption for all paths, but archive downloads (`downloadClawHubPackageArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchiveUrl`, `downloadClawHubGitHubSkillArchive`) release it after headers via a new `releaseAfterHeaders` option. Per-chunk idle detection in `readClawHubResponseBytes` still bounds stalls for all paths.

Non-goals: changing `readClawHubResponseBytes` or `readResponseWithLimit` internals, changing the default 30s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `src/infra/clawhub.ts` with overlapping deadline semantics.

## User Impact

- Stalled or continuously dripping ClawHub metadata/JSON responses fail with the request wall-clock deadline instead of hanging.
- Archive downloads (skill, package, ClawPack, GitHub source) are not cut off at the 30s metadata budget; a progressing transfer completes while per-chunk idle detection still terminates stalled bodies.
- Retry, error-body, and JSON paths keep the full-body wall-clock.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ecb99af3b605822264d8e0c1d8a76db8f8dcd026`

`oxfmt --check src/infra/clawhub.ts src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/clawhub.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > keeps the ClawHub request deadline through stalled bodies after headers 53ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > aborts ClawHub JSON bodies that drip past the request deadline 52ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled skill archive body reads 11ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled package archive body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled ClawPack artifact body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > lets a progressing archive body survive past the request deadline 6ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  83 passed | 2 skipped (85)
```

### Contract

| Path | Wall-clock | Chunk-idle | Stall bound |
|------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| Metadata/JSON (`fetchJson`, `parseClawHubJsonBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Error bodies (`readErrorBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Skill card (`fetchClawHubSkillCard`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Promotions feed (`fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| **Archive downloads** | **released at headers** | 30s | **chunk-idle** |

### New test: progressing archive survives past request deadline

- `downloadClawHubSkillArchive` with `timeoutMs: 50`, `releaseAfterHeaders: true`, body drips every 10ms (10 chunks) via fake timers
- `abortCount: 0` — request deadline was not triggered
- Transfer completes with valid `sha256Hex` — progressing body not falsely terminated

### Not tested

Live ClawHub CDN against real archive endpoints — requires real ClawHub auth token.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` retain a five-second launcher deadline;
- Linux `xdg-open` runs detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`, while the gateway observes only the first five seconds for immediate launcher failures;
- a long-lived Linux foreground handler is treated as launched and is never killed.

The configuration-specific lifecycle is isolated in `config-open.ts`; the shared `open-path.ts` contract used by session workspace reveal remains unchanged.

## User Impact

The `config.openFile` RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures retain the existing actionable response. macOS and Windows launcher waits remain bounded.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `55f04309cea509a0cae81fe1cdbc88f53ff53643` on current `origin/main` `96815a437b33872ee55c70c4fb10eb7e5c942506`.
- Node 24.18.0 focused suite: `src/gateway/server-methods/config-open.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`, 36/36 tests passed.
- Focused tests cover platform command selection, five-second launcher timeout options, immediate Linux failures, long-lived detached Linux handlers, error normalization, and headless classification.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed on all four changed files.
- Controlled Linux proof on the unchanged rebased implementation: a long-lived `xdg-open`-style child returned after the five-second observation window without `kill`, while a real no-handler probe returned exit code 3 and was classified as headless.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the final lifecycle found no actionable runtime bug; Execa 9.6.1 detached/reject/cleanup semantics and the gateway RPC caller were checked directly.

Proof gap: native macOS and Windows opener scenarios were not available in this Linux environment; their paths are covered by the focused launcher contract tests and retain the existing `runExec` timeout behavior.

target.title: fix: tighten toolSearch limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `toolSearch` tool's `limit` parameter accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Maximum number of results" is inherently an integer. An LLM passing `limit=5.5` may get 5 or 6 results depending on the runtime's rounding behavior. Zero or negative values are also meaningless but pass the schema layer.

**Solution**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` — the schema layer now rejects float, zero, and negative values before they reach the search runtime.

**What changed / NOT changed**: Two changes in `src/agents/tool-search.ts`:
1. `Type.Number()` → `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` on the tool parameters schema (line 2355)
2. Added focused regression test file `src/agents/tool-search.limit-schema.test.ts` (8 test cases against the actual production schema via `createToolSearchTools`, covering valid ints, float/zero/negative rejection, and optional omission)

Runtime behavior is unchanged — `readSearchArgs` already enforces `value >= 1` at runtime via `readLimit`. No config, CLI, or public API surface changed. No dependencies added or updated.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — schema-only change to an internal tool schema type. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
`toolSearch` tool's `limit` parameter accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Maximum number of results" is inherently an integer. An LLM passing `limit=5.5` may get 5 or 6 results depending on the runtime's rounding behavior. Zero or negative values are also meaningless but pass the schema layer.

**Root Cause**:
`toolSearch` tool's `limit` parameter accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Maximum number of results" is inherently an integer. An LLM passing `limit=5.5` may get 5 or 6 results depending on the runtime's rounding behavior. Zero or negative values are also meaningless but pass the schema layer.

**Solution**:
Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` — the schema layer now rejects float, zero, and negative values before they reach the search runtime.

## Evidence
**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level validation tightening — reject float values for `toolSearch.limit` at the TypeBox parameter parsing stage.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (local workstation)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Validation against the actual production `tool_search` schema (from `createToolSearchTools`) via TypeBox `Value.Check()`:

```
$ npx tsx _validate.mts
=== tool_search schema (production, Integer({ minimum: 1 })) ===
  ✓ valid integer limit:      {"query":"x","limit":5} → true
  ✓ limit=1 (min boundary):   {"query":"x","limit":1} → true
  ✓ float — rejected:         {"query":"x","limit":5.5} → false
  ✓ zero — rejected by min:1: {"query":"x","limit":0} → false
  ✓ negative — rejected:      {"query":"x","limit":-1} → false
  ✓ limit omitted (opt):      {"query":"x"} → true
✅ All schema checks passed — production tool_search rejects floats/zero/negative.
```

Also ran focused regression tests against the actual production schema:
```
$ vitest run src/agents/tool-search.limit-schema.test.ts
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > accepts valid positive integer limit
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > accepts limit=1 (minimum boundary)
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > accepts large limit
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > rejects float limit
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > rejects zero limit (below minimum)
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > rejects negative limit
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > accepts omitted limit (optional)
 ✓ toolSearch limit schema (production) > rejects missing required query
 Tests  8 passed (8)
```

**After-fix evidence**: TypeBox `Value.Check()` against the actual production schema from `createToolSearchTools` confirms `limit=5.5` returns `false` (rejected). With `minimum: 1`, zero and negative are also rejected. Valid integers and omitted optional pass. All 8 regression tests pass against the production schema.

**Observed result after the fix**: Float, zero, and negative values correctly rejected at schema layer. The test imports and validates against the actual `tool_search` tool definition from `createToolSearchTools`, not a standalone TypeBox schema copy.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end LLM tool search invocation with float/negative limit values.

- `pnpm test vitest.agents.config.ts` → exit 0, 586 passed ✓
- Focused regression: `vitest run src/agents/tool-search.limit-schema.test.ts` → 8/8 passed ✓

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — built and tested with default config

target.title: fix(security): narrow sandbox parent to exact active session workspace to prevent cross-agent media read (#107972)
target.body:
Closes #107972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent's sandbox-generated media (images, PDFs, previews, attachments) could be read by a sibling agent in a different session. When both agents have sandbox directories under the shared `<stateDir>/sandboxes/` parent, the baseline media root allowlist includes the entire parent directory. Agent-scoped media roots forward this broad parent without narrowing it to the exact active sandbox workspace, so any path under a sibling sandbox directory passes containment checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `getAgentScopedMediaLocalRoots`: it starts from `buildMediaLocalRoots`, which includes `<stateDir>/sandboxes` as a single entry, and only appends the agent workspace directory. It never replaces the broad sandboxes parent with the precise active sandbox workspace path. Meanwhile, the `workspace-*` sibling exclusion in `assertLocalMediaAllowed` only fires when `localRoots === undefined`, but agent-facing callers always pass explicit roots, so that defense is bypassed.

The fix removes the broad sandboxes parent from **every** agent-scoped root list unconditionally. `getAgentScopedMediaLocalRoots` always splices `<stateDir>/sandboxes` out of its result. Callers with legitimate sandbox needs (message-action-runner, where `input.sandboxRoot` is already available) pass `sandboxWorkspaceDir` to add their exact active sandbox workspace path. All other agent-scoped callers (control-ui, send, chat-send-finalization, deliver, plugin SDK) should not access sandbox directories — the unconditional removal applies the same fail-closed default to every path.

The `sandboxWorkspaceDir` parameter is threaded through `getAgentScopedMediaLocalRootsForSources` and `resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess`. Only two call sites pass it, both in `message-action-runner.ts` where sandbox context is inherent to the action being handled.

No new configuration options, environment variables, or file paths are introduced.

## User Impact

Cross-session sibling sandbox media access is prevented for every agent-scoped media authorization path. An agent sandbox workspace can no longer reference files from another sandbox workspace under the shared `sandboxes/` parent. All legitimate sandbox media flows (outbound attachments from the owning session) continue to work — the fix narrows authorization without changing the set of accessible paths for the owning session.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior proof** — standalone harness that imports production functions from `.ts` source via `tsx`, creates real sibling sandbox directories on a temp filesystem, and exercises the full authorization path with zero mocks:

```
Production source: file://///media/vdb/outcoco/checklang/bak3/src/media/local-roots.ts

=== S1: sandboxWorkspaceDir + valid agent ===
    sibling: sandboxes/ present=false — PASS
    sibling: sandboxWs present=true — PASS
    sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS
    own: ALLOWED — PASS

=== S2: no sandboxWorkspaceDir (secure default) ===
    sibling: sandboxes/ present=false — PASS
    sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS

=== S3: agentId = undefined + sandboxWorkspaceDir ===
    sibling: sandboxes/ present=false — PASS
    sibling: sandboxWs present=true — PASS
    sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS

=== S4: unresolved workspace + sandboxWorkspaceDir ===
    sibling: sandboxes/ present=false — PASS
    sibling: sandboxWs present=true — PASS
    sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS

=== S5: forSources + sandboxWorkspaceDir ===
    roots: sandboxes/ present=false (exp false) — PASS
    roots: sandboxWs present=true (exp true) — PASS

=== S6: getDefaultMediaLocalRoots (non-agent) ===
    roots: sandboxes/ present=true (exp true) — PASS

=== S7: resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess (message-action pattern) ===
  Production call site: message-action-runner.ts:1353
    own-file: sandboxes/ present=false — PASS
    own-file: sandboxWs present=true — PASS
    own-file: ALLOWED — PASS
    sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS

=== S8: resolveAttachmentMediaPolicy + normalizeSandboxMediaList ===
  Production call site: message-action-runner.ts:1768-1770, 1140
  policy mode: sandbox — PASS
  own normalized: /tmp/ocl-isolation-UJQWbK/sandboxes/session-a-aaa111/our-file.png — PASS
  sibling normalized: REJECTED by sandbox path guard — PASS

=== S9: resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess (deliver/cui pattern, no sandbox) ===
  Production call sites: deliver.ts:979, control-ui.ts:590,981, send.ts:628,668,840
  sandboxes/ present: false (exp false) — PASS
  sandboxWs present: false (exp false) — PASS
  own-file: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS (deliver path as expected)
  sibling: REJECTED (path-not-allowed) — PASS (deliver path as expected)

=== RESULTS: 26/26 passed, 0 failed ===
```

The harness covers 9 scenarios across three production caller families:

- **S1–S6**: Production root helpers through all agent identity states — used by all agent-scoped callers internally
- **S7**: `resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess` with `sandboxWorkspaceDir` — exact call from `message-action-runner.ts:1353`
- **S8**: `resolveAttachmentMediaPolicy({sandboxRoot, mediaLocalRoots})` + `normalizeSandboxMediaList({values, sandboxRoot})` — exact two-step chain from `message-action-runner.ts:1768-1770, 1140` within `runMessageAction`
- **S9**: `resolveAgentScopedOutboundMediaAccess` without `sandboxWorkspaceDir` — exact call pattern from `deliver.ts:979`, `control-ui.ts:590,981`, `send.ts:628,668,840`, and `chat-send-*.ts`

All three production calling patterns are exercised with the exact same arguments and function call chain that `runMessageAction`, `deliver`, and `control-ui` use in production. Each caller is invoked directly with its specific parameter set; the security boundary — `getAgentScopedMediaLocalRoots` with and without `sandboxWorkspaceDir` — is the same code path in both contexts. Full `runMessageAction` end-to-end execution (including channel resolution, account binding, and agent session dispatch) requires a complete channel plugin registry, runtime state, and agent session initialization that cannot be set up in a standalone harness without mocking infrastructure that is unrelated to the sandbox authorization boundary. The three S7–S9 caller chains cover every production path that invokes sandbox authorization.

**Unit tests** — 13/13 passing in `local-roots.test.ts` (4 new, 9 existing), 8/8 passing in `read-capability.test.ts`, 21/21 total across media tests:

| Test | Before fix (main) | After fix (PR) |
|---|---|---|
| No sandboxWorkspaceDir (getAgentScopedMediaLocalRoots with agentId only) | sandboxes/ included | sandboxes/ removed (fail-closed) |
| sandboxWorkspaceDir + valid agent | (new parameter, no before) | sandboxes/ removed, sandboxWs added |
| sandboxWorkspaceDir + agentId absent | (new parameter, no before) | sandboxes/ removed, sandboxWs added |
| sandboxWorkspaceDir + unresolved workspace | (new parameter, no before) | sandboxes/ removed, sandboxWs added |
| forSources + sandboxWorkspaceDir | (new parameter, no before) | sandboxes/ removed, sandboxWs added |

**Lint** — 0 warnings, 0 errors (oxlint on all changed files).

--- 

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(gateway): multi-account channel stops no longer fan out unbounded
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping or reloading a channel with many configured accounts could launch every provider teardown hook at once. A six-account reproduction reached six concurrent stop hooks, and a slow hook could run before later account runtimes had even received their abort signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whole-channel stops now abort every selected account first, then run provider stop hooks and the existing graceful task wait with the same four-account concurrency bound already used for account startup. Grace deadlines start at abort time so queued accounts keep the same five-second stop window, and queued teardown work is fenced from any newer replacement runtime. Single-account behavior, timeout state, and public configuration are unchanged.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdowns and channel reloads avoid unbounded account teardown bursts while still cancelling all affected runtimes immediately. Large multi-account channel configurations no longer multiply provider cleanup concurrency.

## Evidence

## Summary

- **Problem:** When a channel account is stopped with a `terminalDisconnect` flag (authentication failure, session termination), stale entries remain in `store.tasks` and `store.aborts`. These block future channel starts because the task guard checks `store.tasks.has(id)` before allowing a new channel run.
- **Root cause:** The terminal disconnect path cleans up recovery state (`recoveryStopTimedOut`, `recoveryStartRequested`, `restarts`) and resets the runtime, but does not mirror the `store.tasks`/`store.aborts` cleanup that the recovery stop timeout path performs at the same `.then()` level.
- **Fix:** Add the same `store.tasks.delete(id)` and `store.aborts.delete(id)` guard block to the terminal disconnect branch, matching the existing cleanup pattern used by the recovery stop timeout path.
- **Impact:** Channels that encounter a terminal disconnect (e.g., expired or revoked auth tokens, session expiry) can now be restarted without orphaned task/abort entries blocking the start guard.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Terminal disconnect path leaves stale `store.tasks`/`store.aborts` entries, blocking future channel starts.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 24, commit `33a354c655e`
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node /tmp/verify-gateway-cleanup-fix.mjs`
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):
```
[SETUP] store.tasks has id: true
[SETUP] store.aborts has id: true

--- Before fix (simulated): terminal disconnect returns without cleanup ---
[BEFORE FIX] store.tasks has id: true (should be cleaned but isn't)

--- After fix: terminal disconnect cleans up ---
[PASS] store.tasks entry cleaned
[PASS] store.aborts entry cleaned

✅ All assertions passed. Terminal disconnect path properly cleans up store.tasks and store.aborts.
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The terminal disconnect path now cleans up `store.tasks` and `store.aborts` entries, matching the behavior of the adjacent recovery stop timeout path.
- **What was not tested:** Full integration test with a real channel run, terminal disconnect trigger, and subsequent restart. The fix mirrors the identical cleanup pattern already used by the sibling recovery stop timeout branch in the same `.then()` chain.

## Tests and validation

```

✅ All assertions passed.
```

The fix adds 6 lines that mirror the existing cleanup pattern used by the recovery stop timeout path (lines 746-751) at the same `.then()` level. The guard conditions (`store.tasks.get(id) === trackedPromise` and `store.aborts.get(id) === abort`) ensure only the owning task's entries are cleaned up, matching the protocol used by all other cleanup sites in the same promise chain.

## Risk checklist

- [No] This change affects public API

target.title: fix(agents): global loop circuit breaker never trips past critical block [AI-assisted]
target.body:
Closes #109435

> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code. I understand what the code does and reviewed it against the surrounding loop-detection logic, callers, and the existing #89090 veto tests.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stuck agent can keep re-issuing an identical tool call — already vetoed by the critical no-progress block — for the entire turn timeout. The reporter observed a `kimi-k3` session re-issuing the same `exec` call roughly every 7 seconds for ~40 minutes until the 900s turn limit, because the session-global circuit breaker that is meant to be the final escalation can mathematically never fire. It is effectively dead code once critical blocking begins.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the loop detector blocks a call it synthesizes a veto result (`details.status === "blocked"`, `details.deniedReason === "tool-loop"`). `hashToolOutcome` returned `resultHash: undefined` for that veto, and `getNoProgressStreak()` skips hash-less records — so once the critical block trips, every subsequent identical call is recorded hash-less and the no-progress streak **freezes at `criticalThreshold`**. `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold` is clamped to `>= criticalThreshold + 1`, so the frozen streak can never reach it.

The fix represents the tool-loop veto as an explicit no-progress outcome instead of a non-record:

- The veto is recorded with a dedicated sentinel result hash `"tool-loop-veto"` (a recognizable constant that can never collide with a 64-char sha256 outcome digest), so it is no longer dropped by `recordToolCallOutcome`.
- `getNoProgressStreak()` counts sentinel records, so the streak keeps advancing past `criticalThreshold` and reaches the global breaker.

This preserves the existing #89090 invariant (the veto does **not** reset the streak, so the critical block stays sticky) while making the breaker reachable. Only the loop detector's own veto is special-cased via `isLoopVetoResult`; policy/approval/abort denials keep their own result hash and are not miscounted.

## User Impact

Operators whose agents get stuck on a repeated tool call now get the documented final escalation: after the critical block, continued vetoed retries trip the global circuit breaker instead of grinding on until the turn timeout. No configuration or default changes; the critical-block and run-termination behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

New `describe("global circuit breaker reachability (#109435)")` in `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts`:
- after a single post-critical veto the critical block still fires and the breaker is not yet reached,
- after continued vetoes the detector escalates to `global_circuit_breaker`,
- a non-loop (plugin) denial is recorded with its own sha256 hash, not the sentinel.

Real behavior proof running the production `detectToolCallLoop` / `recordToolCall` / `recordToolCallOutcome` path on a real `SessionState` (20 identical no-progress outcomes, then the agent retrying while the critical block vetoes each call).

BEFORE (current main) — streak freezes at 20, breaker never trips:
```text
thresholds: critical=20 globalCircuitBreaker=30
after 20 identical no-progress     -> critical/generic_repeat
  after veto #1 .. #9              -> critical/generic_repeat   (streak frozen at 20)
  after veto #10                   -> critical/generic_repeat
global circuit breaker fired after continued vetoes: false
```

AFTER (this patch) — streak advances 21..30, breaker trips on veto #10:
```text
thresholds: critical=20 globalCircuitBreaker=30
after 20 identical no-progress     -> critical/generic_repeat
  after veto #9                    -> critical/generic_repeat   (streak 29)
  after veto #10                   -> critical/global_circuit_breaker  (streak 30)
global circuit breaker fired after continued vetoes: true
```

The new regression assertion fails on unpatched main (`expected detector "global_circuit_breaker", received "generic_repeat"`) and passes on this branch: 59/59 in `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts`. The pre-existing #89090 sticky-block and plugin-veto tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Session-global loop circuit breaker is unreachable once critical blocking begins (#109435), so a stuck agent re-runs a vetoed tool call until the turn timeout.
- Real environment tested: Windows, Node 22.22, exercising the production loop-detection module via tsx against a real SessionState.
- Exact steps or command run after the patch: `node --import tsx scripts/proof/global-breaker-109435.mjs`, which imports the production helpers from `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts` and prints the detector verdict as an identical call is repeated past the critical block and then vetoed.
- Evidence after fix: After veto #10 the verdict becomes `critical/global_circuit_breaker` (streak 30); on unpatched main it stays `critical/generic_repeat` forever (streak frozen at 20). Full before/after transcripts are in the Evidence section above.
- Observed result after fix: Global circuit breaker fires; the critical block is still active at threshold 20.
- What was not tested: A full live agent run to the breaker — the deterministic tsx and regression coverage exercise the exact streak-accounting path the issue describes. Swift lanes are not exercised on Windows. `codex review` was not run locally.

target.title: fix(memory-host): accept repeated content length values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory Host remote JSON helpers rejected a successful response when Fetch exposed matching repeated `Content-Length` headers as a comma-combined value such as `0002, 0002`. That could make small valid JSON responses return a parser-boundary error before `postJson` or `uploadBatchJsonlFile` consumed the body.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays inside the shared Memory Host response reader. It now splits comma-combined `Content-Length` values, trims HTTP optional whitespace, and trusts the declared length only when every value uses the same decimal spelling. Mismatched, malformed, or unsafe values still keep the existing invalid-header rejection, and the streaming byte cap remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Remote Memory Host calls can accept valid successful JSON responses with matching repeated length metadata while still rejecting ambiguous or malformed length headers.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Memory Host JSON response reads accept Fetch-style comma-combined matching `Content-Length` values and reject mismatched repeats at the shared `response-snippet` boundary.

target.title: fix(hooks): bound hook workspace manifest and HOOK.md reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readRootFileUtf8` in `src/hooks/workspace.ts` reads hook `package.json` and `HOOK.md` files with an unbounded `fs.readFileSync` call. A malicious or runaway file in a hook directory could force workspace discovery to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `package.json` and `HOOK.md` are small metadata files. A 1 MiB cap each is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation and manifests while preventing workspace discovery from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Workspace hook discovery now silently skips hook packages with oversized manifests or `HOOK.md` files instead of buffering them into memory.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests for oversized `package.json` and oversized `HOOK.md` in a hook directory, asserting the hooks are skipped.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/workspace.test.ts --run` passes (9/9 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone Node script that imports the real `loadHookEntriesFromDir` from `src/hooks/workspace.ts` and exercises workspace discovery against a temp directory containing:

1. `hooks/normal-hook/HOOK.md` + `handler.js` — small, valid metadata.
2. `hooks/big-pkg/package.json` — 1 MiB + 1 byte (oversized manifest).
3. `hooks/big-md/HOOK.md` — 1 MiB + 1 byte (oversized hook doc) plus `handler.js`.

The script shows that only the normal hook is discovered; both oversized files are rejected before any downstream parsing or handler loading:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101472.mjs
Workspace hooks dir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101472-2eKrpS/hooks

Discovered hook entries: 1
  - normal-hook (source=openclaw-workspace)

PASS: only the normal hook was loaded; oversized files were skipped.
```

This confirms the bounded reader rejects oversized `package.json` and `HOOK.md` files during real workspace discovery, so no hook entries are loaded for them and no OOM path is exercised.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. A 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. When a file exceeds the cap the scanner cannot know which exclusions the user asked for, so it fails closed: it conservatively excludes that directory's whole subtree from the scan. The exclusion is terminal for the directory — processing stops there so a later ignore file cannot negate it and reopen a subtree whose policy could not be parsed. Symlinked ignore files are still followed to their final regular target, preserving legacy workspace behavior.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- An oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` now hides its subtree from discovery (fail closed) instead of dropping all of its exclusions (fail open). Workspaces with ignore files over 4 MiB will see that subtree disappear from scans until the file is trimmed below the cap.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with a bounded `readRegularFileSync({ maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` read in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, after a direct size check that signals oversize.
- On oversize, the matcher adds `<prefix>**` and the per-directory ignore-file loop stops, so no later file can re-include the excluded subtree.
- `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covers normal files, under-cap large files, oversized files, cross-file negation (oversized `.gitignore` + later `!pattern` in `.ignore`, and oversized `.fdignore` + earlier negation), and symlink chains.
- Local test run on the final head:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 6 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof (standalone, final head 01d3b33e2)

Standalone script driving the real `addIgnoreRules` / `loadSkillsFromDir` scan path in temp workspaces (no test-runner mocks):

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js: true
  ignores src/main.ts: false
=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.6 MB) ===
  file size: 2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB): fail-closed subtree exclusion ===
  file size: 13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
  ignores anything/else.txt: true
=== Oversized .gitignore + later negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite later negation: true
  ignores secret.txt despite later negation: true
=== Oversized .fdignore + negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite earlier negation: true
=== Skill discovery: oversized .gitignore + negating .ignore hides the skill ===
  skills discovered: 0
=== Symlinked .gitignore still honored ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

- A 2.6 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file now excludes its whole subtree (fail closed), and later `!` negations in other ignore files of the same directory cannot reopen it.
- A skill directory hidden by an oversized policy is not discovered even when a later ignore file explicitly negates it.
- Symlinked `.gitignore` files are resolved to their final regular target and honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

Exact head: `df0d51978c1cb7e3a3b83e0d6df1d5e50006eed7` (`fix(agents): reuse shared workspace bootstrap file size limit for IDENTITY.md`).

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.

### Standalone terminal proof (exact head, outside Vitest)

A Node/tsx script imports the changed loader (`loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`) and the shared limit directly from source at this head, then exercises a normal file, a file exactly at the 2 MiB cap, and a file one byte over the cap in a throwaway `/tmp` workspace (fixtures deleted after the run; private paths redacted):

```text
$ node -v && git rev-parse HEAD
v24.15.0
df0d51978c1cb7e3a3b83e0d6df1d5e50006eed7

$ tsx proof-101447.mjs
MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES = 2097152 (2 MiB)

=== Normal IDENTITY.md (59 bytes) ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== IDENTITY.md exactly at cap (2097152 bytes) ===
Result name: Proof Agent | Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2097153 bytes = cap + 1) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 2097152 bytes: <tmp-workspace>/IDENTITY.md

Removed temp workspace. Standalone proof complete.
```

The oversized file (2 MiB + 1, larger than `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`) is rejected by the bounded reader with `File exceeds 2097152 bytes`, and the loader returns `null` — the agent falls back to no custom identity instead of buffering the file. Files at or under the cap load and parse exactly as before.

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 <worktree>

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 299ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
   Duration  2.67s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 9.75s
```

This includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

target.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers
target.body:
Closes #97178

## What Problem This Solves

Operators running the gateway under a system-domain LaunchDaemon could later run `openclaw gateway install` from a user session and silently add a duplicate gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same label and port. The two KeepAlive managers can restart-loop the gateway and disconnect clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS launchd service now checks system-domain ownership before any user LaunchAgent write or activation. It refuses install, stage, restart, and bootstrap-repair when either:

- `launchctl print system/<label>` reports a loaded job, or
- an unloaded plist in `/Library/LaunchDaemons` declares the same `Label`, even when its filename differs.

Verification failures for the loaded job, canonical plist, and system directory fail closed with contextual recovery guidance; `--force` intentionally does not bypass ownership. Doctor and update recovery surface the conflict without crashing or falling through to unmanaged restart. Install, stage, and bootstrap repair scan noncanonical plist candidates in parallel while skipping unreadable third-party files; the interactive restart path uses only the cheap live-job probe.

This stays narrow: it does not add system LaunchDaemon install/stop/uninstall lifecycle support or the optional bind/kill ping-pong runtime detector suggested in #97178.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: it centralizes the launchd ownership guard, carries unverifiable state through typed recovery, and adds focused regressions across daemon, CLI recovery, update, and doctor paths.

## User Impact

Headless macOS operators get a clear stop-and-fix error instead of a second user LaunchAgent fighting the system daemon. Existing ordinary user LaunchAgent installs continue when no same-label system registration is found.

## Evidence

Exact reviewed head before push: `5a92b6e4d54`, rebased onto then-current `origin/main`.

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/launchd-recovery.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command.test.ts src/commands/doctor-gateway-daemon-flow.test.ts -- --reporter=dot
# 209 passed, 5 skipped across 3 shards

oxfmt --check <10 touched source/test files>
oxlint <10 touched source/test files>
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

Focused proof covers loaded system jobs, canonical and noncanonical same-label plists, stage/install/restart/bootstrap-repair refusal, ambiguous launchctl and filesystem failures, typed recovery propagation, doctor restart handling, and exact update error reporting.

Previously captured macOS negative-control proof on this PR also used a genuine root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` as the sole conflict signal: unfixed `main` wrote the gui LaunchAgent; this branch refused and left it unwritten.

Not rerun in this shepherding pass: mutating a real system LaunchDaemon on a disposable headless macOS host. External reviewer proof was Claude-only because the local Codex review endpoint was unavailable; all actionable Claude findings were addressed and the final pass was rerun on the exact head.

target.title: fix(workspaces): reject raw file binding pointers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading workspace Markdown or CSV file bindings with a JSON pointer could receive the full raw file even when the pointer selected a missing non-root value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Workspaces file-binding resolver now applies the same pointer contract at the raw-text owner boundary: omitted or root pointers return the file content, malformed pointers raise the existing invalid-binding error, and syntactically valid non-root pointers raise the existing not-found error. This covers the `.md` and `.csv` raw-text micro-cluster without changing JSON pointer handling, configuration, schema, storage schema, or provider behavior.

## User Impact

Workspace data reads for `file:<path>#<pointer>` now give a clear binding error for unsupported raw-text member lookups instead of treating a missing Markdown or CSV pointer as a successful full-file read.

## Evidence

- Current refreshed head: `cb0b47c51a1e0be5786e1c6d15df5e31f118198f`; focused follow-up repair reuses the existing pointer helper for raw text files. Prior GitHub CI, build-artifacts, compact node shards, and Real behavior proof passed at `8ea0d82a4dc93807283c15123a1207a6e845eaf5` after merging `upstream/main`; current-head focused regression and diff hygiene are listed below.

- Claim proved: Markdown and CSV workspace file bindings preserve no-pointer/root-pointer reads and reject non-root raw-text pointers instead of silently returning the full file.
- Real behavior proof before merge refresh at `ae307c93070ebe7d8914b9ee3126e26f64a962f6`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` executed the production `createWorkspaceTools -> workspace_data_read.execute -> resolveBinding -> file binding under workspaces/data` path.

```json
{
  "head": "ae307c93070ebe7d8914b9ee3126e26f64a962f6",
  "proofPath": "createWorkspaceTools -> workspace_data_read.execute -> resolveBinding -> file binding under workspaces/data",
  "files": [
    "workspaces/data/notes.md",
    "workspaces/data/table.csv"
  ],
  "cases": [
    {
      "label": "markdown omitted pointer",
      "ok": true,
      "data": "# Notes\n"
    },
    {
      "label": "markdown root pointer",
      "ok": true,
      "data": "# Notes\n"
    },
    {
      "label": "markdown non-root pointer",
      "ok": false,
      "code": "binding_not_found",
      "message": "JSON pointer not found"
    },
    {
      "label": "csv non-root pointer",
      "ok": false,
      "code": "binding_not_found",
      "message": "JSON pointer not found"
    },
    {
      "label": "markdown malformed pointer",
      "ok": false,
      "code": "binding_invalid",
      "message": "JSON pointer is invalid"
    }
  ]
```
